rubrics.justification: The response substantially contradicts the provided laboratory grade of 0DD by describing a fair-quality expanded/full blastocyst around 3-5BC and even possible hatching; this overcalls expansion and cell quality and introduces features not supported by the case data.

It integrates most relevant patient factors well, including age, BMI, ovarian reserve, semen, endometrium, diagnosis, and first-cycle status, and relates them to prognosis despite the embryo-quality misclassification.

The internal logic is generally structured and consistent, but the prognosis and recommendations are built on an incorrect morphological premise, which weakens the validity of the probability estimate.

Recommendations such as SET, standard luteal support, avoiding unnecessary add-ons, and not routinely using PGT-A at age 28 are broadly guideline-consistent, but the embryo grading interpretation is not aligned with Gardner criteria for a 0DD embryo.
Provides practical next steps for transfer management, lifestyle optimization, and future-cycle review, with reasonable nuance about when to escalate testing or protocol changes.
